figures.title: Case 1: which condition is 'better' depends on the outcome
figures.caption: Grey = the paper's d_z and 95% CI. Coloured = this run's synthetic learners (generated so the sample d_z match exactly) with bootstrap CIs. Blue = engagement-type outcomes (E), orange = learning (L).

figures.title: Where does the decision flip?
figures.caption: Probability that the gamified condition comes out ahead as the weight moves from engagement to learning. The star is your weighting (B and P weights dropped: Case 1 did not measure them).

figures.title: Case 2: can an AI find who learned by watching engagement?
figures.caption: Left: one synthetic cohort, engagement vs perceived-knowledge gain (note the pile-up at the scale top). Right: share of the top-third gainers that a system ranking learners by engagement would pick, by how strongly engagement tracks gains (300 synthetic cohorts per point).

figures.title: Case 2: one intervention, four 'success' numbers
figures.caption: Standardized effects from the paper's reported numbers. Persistence is not measured yet (T2 ongoing): the hatched bar is your retention assumption times the learning effect.
